title: Tenant-sampled link router for Dedicated & Private observability
creator: Lucas Chen
description: Implement a tenant-aware sampling and trace-linking router for Dedicated and Private deployments. The router should allow per-customer sampling policies (rate, probabilistic, adaptive) without leaking tenant identifiers across shared telemetry pipelines, support edge-side and aggregator-side sampling modes, and maintain trace continuity for downstream debugging and latency/error dashboards. This ticket covers design, a lightweight sidecar prototype for on-prem collectors, integration with the Console sampling UI, and performance validation against our existing ingest path.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant sampling policies can be configured via Console and propagated to on-prem collectors and Dedicated perimeter proxies
Sampling decisions preserve trace context and span IDs so traces stitched across customer-private and hosted segments remain queryable
No tenant-identifying metadata is written into shared telemetry topics when tenant-obfuscation mode is enabled
End-to-end P99 latency impact of the ingest path is <= 10ms additional overhead at 95th percentile under representative load (validated with load tests)
Integration tests cover edge-side sampling, aggregator-side re-sampling, and fallback to global-default policy
Documentation and runbook updated: Confluence design doc, Console UI guide, and on-call playbook for sampling regressions
comments: 2025-01-28 Lucas Chen: Initial scoping and prototype plan. Will evaluate sidecar vs centralized controller trade-offs. Linked a strawman Confluence design.
2025-02-04 Marisol Rivera: Prototype sidecar implemented for Linux onprem collector (k8s DaemonSet). Observed ~6ms median overhead and ~9ms p95 under 500rps with batching=16.
2025-02-12 Security review: flagged tenant-obfuscation mode for additional audit; added requirement to strip raw tenant IDs from Kafka topic keys when obfuscation enabled.
2025-02-20 Eng-arch sync: Decided to implement hybrid model — default edge-side sampling with optional central policy rollout via signed manifests to reduce control-plane chatter.

2025-02-28 QA: Added test plan for trace continuity validation across customer private bridge -> hosted pipeline. Found an issue where sampling decision metadata was not propagated in OTLP envelope; patching now (PR #8421).

2025-03-05 Marisol Rivera: Performance run completed for dedicated pool at 2k rps; p95 overhead ~11ms when collecting full spans. Switching to KV-only span compression in next iteration to hit acceptance criteria.
notes: Design trade-offs: central controller simplifies global policy changes but increases control-plane dependency and cross-tenant risk; sidecar/hybrid reduces blast radius and scales with existing collector footprint.

Privacy constraint: when tenant-obfuscation is active, sampling decisions must be deterministic but derived from a hashed tenant slug stored only in the customer control plane; do not emit unhashed slugs to shared topics.

Migration plan: roll out in three phases — (1) opt-in per-customer sidecar, (2) enable Console policy editor and signed manifests, (3) global enable with conservative defaults and monitoring dashboards.
Follow-ups: UX ticket for Console policy templating (PM backlog), and a separate ENG ticket to add signed-manifest verification into Collector start-up flow.
